anomalies.observed: On the 'WATER LEVEL SENSOR/SWITCHES' sheet, under the 'Water Height Sensor' heading, the TF-Luna LiDAR (PR1, PB_1.25mm, with mating connector P1) has its board connector H4 wired: pin 2 (SDA) and pin 3 (SCL) are connected by wires to the main-bus labels I2C_SDA and I2C_SCL (the same non-isolated bus that carries R3/R4 pull-ups, the EZO-RTD and the ADM3260 primary sides). No trigger/echo (HC-SR04 style) interface appears anywhere on the sheet.
anomalies.expected: The specification states PR1 is a schematic/BOM-only part that is not connected to any net ('on_board: no', all pins 'free'), and that the water-level sensing that is actually wired is an HC-SR04-style ultrasonic sensor read on two ESP32 GPIOs. The drawing should therefore show PR1 unconnected and an ultrasonic trigger/echo interface instead.

evidence.quote: the r2 netlist shows PR1 with on_board: no, in_bom: yes, and all four pins (VCC, SDA, SCL, GND) typed free — i.e., it is not connected to any net in this design.
The water-level sensing that is actually wired and actually used by firmware is an HC-SR04-style ultrasonic sensor read on two ESP32 GPIOs (see §4).
Water Height Sensor: PR1 LIDAR / P1 PB_1.25mm, connector H4 with SDA/SCL wired to I2C_SDA and I2C_SCL (WATER LEVEL SENSOR/SWITCHES sheet)

anomalies.impact: The water-level interface is an I2C LiDAR rather than the intended GPIO ultrasonic sensor, so the board cannot perform the water-level sensing the design intends; additionally an unintended (firmware-unused) TF-Luna device is placed on the shared main I2C bus with the EZO-RTD and the isolator primary sides.

parsed.summary: The power train, ADM3260 isolation, TMC2209 stepper drivers and pump/valve drivers match the specification, but the water-level sensing path is wrong: PR1 (TF-Luna LiDAR) is wired onto the main I2C bus via H4, whereas the spec states PR1 is unconnected and water level is sensed by an HC-SR04 on GPIO4/GPIO5, which is absent from the schematic.
